judgments.reasoning_cat1: A block-capital notice stating claims must be 'FIRST MADE ... AND REPORTED ... DURING THE POLICY PERIOD' with no mention of the extended reporting period; the flat statement is capable of being read as an operative condition or as a mere caption.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared perfectly with Insuring Agreement I.A./I.B. and Section VIII, which allow a claim to be reported during an 'extended reporting period' after the policy period ends.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration statement listing the documents constituting the policy; nothing in it carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the endorsement list and with IX.K (Changes and Assignment), which likewise requires changes to be by attached endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical is garbled ('litem, 3.a.', stray commas) and '100 % minimum-earned' is a percentage stated in a slot elsewhere called a 'premium percentage', leaving what is earned on day one arguably uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly against IX.A.3, which contemplates 'remaining unearned premium' earned pro rata and a pro rata refund within thirty days — impossible if 100% is minimum-earned at inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same block-capital notice as the Declarations version; the unqualified 'reported ... during the policy period' overstates the reporting condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in emphasis with I.A./I.B. and Section VIII.B., which deem claims reported in an extended reporting period to have been reported on the last day of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple signpost that quoted terms are defined in Section V.; no term in it is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements add defined terms outside Section V. (e.g. 'business interruption loss', 'product pollution'), a minor mismatch with the statement that definitions live in Section V.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/reliance recital; 'in reliance upon all statements made in the Application' is boilerplate rather than genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with IX.F. Representations and the Fraud or Misrepresentation exclusion; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Coverages being 'identified on the Declarations'; plain and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplemental coverages are added by endorsement rather than 'identified on the Declarations', a small tension with II.G. which expressly contemplates Supplemental Coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' is a genuinely contestable phrase for a continuing or creeping pollution condition, as is 'arising out of'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This same subsection is deleted and replaced in its entirety twice — by Endorsement 5.II (retroactive-date version) and again by Endorsement 10.I (transportation version) — leaving two competing replacements of one clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' is workable but its boundary against Coverage A's 'in their entirety during' is arguable for conditions straddling inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with I.A. and with Endorsement 5's retroactive-date rewrite of Coverage A, the allocation of a straddling condition between Coverages A and B is not fully resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'satisfactory evidence' and 'the same, continuous, repeated, or related pollution condition' are elastic phrases that decide how many retentions apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the SIR definition (V.AA.) and III.D., though the Catastrophe Management endorsement adds a separate $100,000 retention without expressly reconciling with this one-retention rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-condition limit cross-referring to Item 2.b.; the only soft term, 'related pollution condition', is defined by usage throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I expressly deletes and replaces this subsection, so the base text is superseded rather than contradicted, but a reader must notice the replacement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain aggregate-limit statement keyed to Item 2.c.; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2.c. is $9,000,000 while Item 4.'s Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000, so the 'maximum liability' language must be subordinated to II.G. to make sense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror of the Coverage A per-condition limit; mechanical and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded by Endorsement 6.I.E., which adds an undefined 'covered operations' qualifier absent here — a divergence between the two versions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain aggregate limit keyed to Item 3.c.; no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I.F. replaces it and adds 'resulting from covered operations', an undefined limitation, so the two texts do not say the same thing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'subject to Subsections C., D., E. and F.' formula is circular with those subsections, which are themselves made subject to G.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Item 4. figure ($7,000,000) is smaller than the Coverage A aggregate in Item 2.c. ($9,000,000), so the Declarations and this clause cannot both operate at face value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'continuous, repeated, or related' and the deeming of later-reported conditions into 'this policy period' are contestable, and 'no other policy shall respond' purports to bind instruments not before the reader.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations identify this as a renewal of an earlier policy, so the deeming rule interacts with prior-period coverage and with the Known Conditions exclusion in ways not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duty to defend 'a claim to which this insurance applies' is standard, though the trigger for the duty ending on exhaustion or tender is stated compactly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.A. deletes and replaces this subsection with a differently worded exhaustion trigger keyed to the defense sublimit, so the base text no longer operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Selection of legal counsel by the Insurer shall not be done without the consent of the insured' sits oddly with the Insurer's asserted 'right to select', and 'entitled by law to select independent counsel' imports an external standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in tension with Endorsement 6.IV.F., which gives the first named insured the right to select counsel after the defense sublimit is exhausted, and with IX.M. on unreasonable withholding of consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Casting retention of a consultant as both a 'right and the duty' of the insured, subject to the Insurer's prior written consent, is internally awkward but its operation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.III.C. deletes and replaces this subsection in its entirety, and VII.C. (also replaced) states the consent rule again in slightly different words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence erosion rule; nothing to construe on its own wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.D. replaces it with a dedicated defense sublimit erosion rule, so the base sentence and the endorsement state different erosion mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens on the insured' is a vague condition on the hammer clause and could be fought over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F. restates a garbled version of the same hammer clause for post-exhaustion claims, creating two overlapping formulations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'located ... within the United States of America' is definite; the only stretch is applying 'located' to a migrating condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the covered-location schedules and with Endorsement 8's US-only non-owned disposal site definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition by cross-reference to endorsement; 'only those rights that are specified by endorsement' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 2 supplies the endorsement contemplated and limits Hoffman Rettig to vicarious liability, matching this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated definition; 'prospective medical monitoring costs' is a slightly unusual inclusion but its scope is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Employers Liability exclusion and the 'claim' definition without evident friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the hygienist to be 'mutually agreed upon', which could deadlock, but the qualification criteria are spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 excludes all fungi and legionella claims and costs, which leaves this fungi-specific definition (and its role in 'remediation costs') with nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'written assertion of a legal right' plus 'including, but not limited to, a government action' is a general-plus-specific formulation whose reach (e.g. regulatory letters, agency directives) is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 8.II and again by Endorsement 11.II, each 'solely with respect to' its own coverage, leaving the operative text layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and closed definition tied to carriers for hire; little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.II deletes Subsection E. and substitutes 'transportation', yet the Vehicles exclusion in the base policy still carves back for 'contingent transportation', a term that no longer exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbering is corrupted (no '1.') and paragraph 2 refers to an Automatic Acquisition Endorsement that is not attached, though the 'if any' saves it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection F. is deleted and replaced in its entirety by both Endorsement 8.I and Endorsement 11.I with materially different texts, so which 'covered location' definition governs is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'imminent and substantial threat' is a standard but evaluative phrase, and the 72-hour window is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The emergency-response carve-out recurs in III.C., VII.C. and VI.H. consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to a 'Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement', with 'if any' making the definition potentially empty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such schedule is attached, so the Contractual Liability exclusion's carve-back for 'environmental indemnity obligations' has nothing to bite on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping list ending in 'guidance document' and 'risk-based corrective action guidance' — whether non-binding agency guidance or an emergency animal-health directive is 'environmental law' is a real question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives 'remediation costs' ('to the extent required by environmental law') and 'government action', so its breadth controls the size of the coverage grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition that does not itself state the length; 'during or subsequent to the end of the policy period' is loose but the operative periods are in Section VIII.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VIII.A. limits entitlement to cancellation or nonrenewal, saying nothing about ordinary expiry, which this open definition does not resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but definite allocation of agency and payment duties; 'sole agent on behalf of all insureds' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits V.S. ('named insured' has the same rights except those reserved here) and IX.A.; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential ('byproducts produced or released by fungi' within the definition of fungi) but the intended breadth is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 deletes fungi from 'pollution condition' and excludes fungi claims outright, leaving this definition and the hygienist machinery orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Depends entirely on 'acting pursuant to the authority of environmental law', which inherits whatever vagueness that term carries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with V.I. and V.D., a directive from an agricultural rather than environmental agency may or may not qualify, which matters for the whole coverage grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of pollutants followed by open categories ('waste materials, including ... medical, infectious and pathological wastes'), a classic ejusdem generis setup.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the 'pollution condition' definition, which Endorsement 12 rewrites while keeping 'illicit abandonment' intact, so this list survives the CAFO amendment unchanged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is circular — 'employee of ... any insured' — and 'while acting within the scope of his or her duties' may or may not qualify all the listed persons.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'insured' sweeps in employees, the Insured vs. Insured exclusion and the Separation of Insureds condition (which speaks only of 'named insureds') do not mesh cleanly with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable legal costs' is evaluative but conventional; the category is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with III.D. and Endorsement 6's dedicated defense sublimit without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'waste with greater than specified quantities' does not say by whom specified, a small but real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used only inside the 'pollution condition' and 'illicit abandonment' definitions and does not clash with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pinned to two named federal statutes; about as definite as a definition gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in W.3 and N.; no friction with other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear cross-reference carve-out for rights reserved to the first named insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with V.K., II.A. (retention payment by 'another named insured') and IX.G.; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long but statute-modelled definition; 'other such resources' is a catch-all after a list, a mild ejusdem generis point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is capped by Endorsement 12.III's $500,000 natural resource damage sublimit and folded into 'property damage'; the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and broad ('any disposal site or recycling facility not owned or operated by an insured'), with no temporal or permitting qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.II.U. deletes and replaces it with a far narrower, condition-laden definition, so the base text is displaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 2. is syntactically broken — 'the period of time following the closing date ... or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date' — and its start point is not stated coherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to an Automatic Acquisition Endorsement that is not attached, and paragraph 3 ('any shorter period resulting from cancellation') interacts with IX.A.2's statement that the cancellation date becomes the end of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core coverage trigger: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including smoke, soot, vapors ...' is the paradigm general-versus-specific list, and whether a biological agent is a 'contaminant' is exactly the kind of fight this wording invites.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 deletes this subsection in its entirety and substitutes a version without the fungi prong and excluding odor, so the base definition is displaced while other clauses (V.C., V.Y.) still assume the fungi prong exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated heads, including 'diminished value of tangible property owned by a third-party'; definite as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Head 4 imports 'natural resource damages' which Endorsement 12 sublimits to $500,000, and the First-Party Property Damage exclusion removes the insured's own property; these fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable expenses ... to the extent required by environmental law' is the pivotal limiter and is genuinely contestable, as is the fungi-specific fallback.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 'environmental law' (V.I.) and on the fungi machinery that Endorsement 12 excludes, and the Insured's Internal Expenses exclusion cuts across the same costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any employee ... responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance' has an uncertain boundary in a large multi-site business.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the Known Conditions, Intentional Non-Compliance and UST exclusions, so its breadth has consequences, but no clause contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straight cross-reference to Items 2.d. and 3.d.; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 adds a separate Catastrophe Management-specific retention without amending this definition, a small layering point the 'as otherwise designated by endorsement' language largely cures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard terrorism definition with evaluative limbs ('appears that the intent is'), but heavily structured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds only the War or Terrorism exclusion and fits it; the Trade Sanctions endorsement is separate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise ten-percent volumetric test with express exclusions for septic tanks and oil/water separators; little room for argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the UST exclusion, which refers to a Schedule of Insured Underground Storage Tanks Endorsement that is not attached; the 'if any' softens that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long catch-all definition ending in 'any use of military force, usurped power or confiscation ... by any government, military or other authority', which could arguably swallow ordinary regulatory seizures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because government-ordered destruction of property could be read into 'confiscation ... by any government', this definition sits uncomfortably beside the coverage grant for government-ordered remediation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad 'arising out of or related to' with a narrow carve-back for asbestos 'discovered in soil or groundwater'; the carve-back's edge is fairly clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the Lead-Based Paint exclusion and does not clash with the coverage grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'liability of others assumed ... through contract' with an 'except if the liability would have attached ... in the absence of such contract' proviso is standard but perennially argued wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-back for 'environmental indemnity obligations' is inoperative because no Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement is attached, an unmatched cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sold, abandoned, or given away' followed by 'or was condemned' is an enumerated list whose treatment of leases or transfers of control is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'This exclusion shall not apply to Coverage B' harmonises with I.B.'s pre-existing-condition trigger, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed employers-liability wording; the numbering is corrupted ('4. Whether an insured may be liable') but the sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'insured' includes employees, this exclusion overlaps the Insured vs. Insured exclusion, but the two are cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion removes 'punitive, exemplary or multiplied damages' and then the carve-back restores punitive and exemplary damages 'where such coverage is insurable by law', leaving the exclusion largely self-cancelling and the applicable law unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The insurability test must be applied under the New York choice of law in IX.J., which the clause does not say, and 'multiplied damages' remain excluded without explanation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in the care, custody, or control of any insured' is a well-worn but genuinely elastic phrase, especially for contract-grower premises.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-back preserving 'remediation costs' interacts with Endorsement 11's non-owned covered locations, where the insured's products sit on someone else's farm; the fit is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'material misrepresentations' and 'which would have affected the Insurer's decision' are evaluative but conventional; the structure is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside IX.F. (warranties), IX.A.2.b. and Endorsement 9's cancellation-for-fraud rule and the Separation of Insureds carve-out, which are consistent with one another.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'services performed by its salaried staff and any employees' is broad, and the carve-back turns on the Insurer's 'sole discretion'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'sole discretion' carve-back is hard to reconcile with IX.M., which says consent required under the Policy shall not be unreasonably withheld or denied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single line with no carve-outs; its breadth is plain even if harsh.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'insured' includes every employee and officer, and because IX.G. expressly disapplies separation of insureds to this exclusion, the clause may bar claims the coverage grant appears to contemplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'intentional disregard of, or knowing, willful, or deliberate non-compliance with' a long list ending in 'instruction of any governmental agency or body' is a general-plus-specific catch-all of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly excepted from Separation of Insureds in IX.G., so one responsible person's conduct defeats every insured — a harsh but stated interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in existence and reported to a responsible person' is ambiguous as to how much must be known, and the carve-back numbering is corrupted ('4.' for '1.').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both carve-backs depend on a Schedule of Known Conditions Endorsement that is not attached, and the exclusion must be read against Coverage B, which exists to cover pre-existing conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirrors the asbestos exclusion with a soil/groundwater carve-back; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the asbestos exclusion and the remediation-cost definition; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a change in the use or operations ... that materially increases the likelihood or severity' is an inherently contestable standard measured against unquoted underwriting materials.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the Application and 'accompanying underwriting materials' which the entire-contract clause names only in part, and is excepted from Separation of Insureds by IX.G.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'naturally occurring materials' with a carve-back for substances present 'as a result of human activities or human processes' is genuinely vague at the margin, which matters greatly at animal-agriculture sites.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against the 'pollution condition' definition and the CAFO endorsement, whether manure, bacteria or a virus is naturally occurring or human-caused is left unresolved by the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple exclusion with a schedule-based carve-back; clear as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.III deletes and replaces this exclusion, and the carve-back refers to a Schedule of Non-Owned Disposal Sites Endorsement that is not attached to the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause joins a 'when ... known' condition by 'and' to two alternatives introduced by 'or', and the second alternative refers to a Schedule of Known Conditions rather than an Insured USTs schedule — the logic is hard to follow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Neither referenced schedule is attached, so the exclusion's carve-outs are empty, and it is excepted from Separation of Insureds in IX.G.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad vehicle exclusion with a conditional carve-back ('if such coverage is added ... by endorsement'); the operative words are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10 deletes this exclusion and substitutes a carve-back for 'transportation', and simultaneously deletes the 'contingent transportation' definition this version relies on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'attributable, whether directly or indirectly' plus an anti-concurrent-causation tail is broad but standard and expressly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on the very wide 'war' definition, so government confiscation-type events could be swept in, but no other clause contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as soon as practicable' and 'all reasonable measures to provide immediate verbal notice' are classic elastic notice standards, and 'Notice should include' is permissive rather than mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations and Insuring Agreements require written reporting during the policy period, whereas this condition sets a practicability standard — the two notice regimes are not expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numbering is garbled (items 3 and 4 lose their numerals) and 'such information and cooperation as it may reasonably require' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the subrogation condition (IX.E.) and the notice condition; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear consent requirement with an emergency-response exception; the sentence structure is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.V deletes and replaces this subsection (mis-citing it as 'Section IV'), and III.C. states an overlapping consent rule, so three texts govern the same ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'make every attempt to mitigate' and 'in the sole judgment of the insurer' are both elastic, and the duty/right asymmetry is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The insurer's unilateral 'sole judgment' power sits against IX.M.'s reasonableness standard and VII.C.'s consent requirement for the insured incurring the same costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entitlement is expressed 'following Cancellation ... or nonrenewal', which on its face says nothing about ordinary expiry of a fixed-term policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That gap matters because I.A./I.B. and VIII.B. assume an extended reporting period is available generally, and Endorsement 7 replaces only subsections C. and D., leaving this trigger untouched.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear deeming provision that limits reinstatement of limits; nothing genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with VIII.C./D. as replaced by Endorsement 7 and with the limits provisions in Section II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence fixing a sixty-day free reporting tail; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 7 deletes and replaces it with ninety days, so the base sixty-day figure is superseded and a reader relying on the policy form alone would be misled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed purchase mechanics; 'not more than two hundred percent' leaves the actual price open but the ceiling is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 7 replaces it with a thirty-three month version, so the thirty-four month figure here no longer operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 1 says the policy 'may be cancelled only by the first named insured' and paragraph 2 then allows the Insurer to cancel — an internal contradiction within one condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3's pro rata unearned-premium refund cannot be reconciled with Item 5's statement that the premium is 100% minimum-earned at inception, and paragraph 2 is itself replaced by Endorsement 9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent of the insured's ability to provide such access' is a soft qualifier but the rights conferred are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The audit right extending three years after 'final termination' fits the extended reporting period regime without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'unless all of the Policy terms have been fully complied with' is a sweeping condition precedent to suit whose strictness is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to square with the Service of Suit Endorsement, under which the company will submit to any court of competent jurisdiction at the insured's request, and with IX.I.'s exclusive New York clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence speaks of 'any other insurance to which this Policy is excess' and of an 'underlying insurer', concepts the rest of this primary policy does not use.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That excess/drop-down language does not fit IX.H., under which this policy is excess only where other collectible insurance happens to exist, nor the SIR structure in Section II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recovery waterfall names the 'insureds' at the first tier and the 'insured' at the third, and 'payments in excess of the limit of coverage' is an odd phrase to apply to a subrogation recovery.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The tiers presuppose the insured may recover its retention last, which fits II.A.'s retention rule but sits awkwardly with IX.H.'s other-insurance escape clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Converting Application statements into 'warranties' is legally consequential but the words themselves are unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Fraud or Misrepresentation exclusion and cancellation ground 2.b., which require materiality, whereas a warranty theory would not — a genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception list cites 'Cancellation condition 2.a.' (non-payment of premium) where the fraud ground is 2.b., which looks like a mechanical mis-citation that changes the clause's effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 9 renumbers nothing but rewrites Cancellation paragraph 2, and the condition speaks only of 'named insureds' while the policy insures a wider class under V.O.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional excess/escape clause; 'valid and collectible' and 'other than a policy specifically written to apply in excess of this Policy' are standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with II.H. ('no other policy shall respond') and IX.D.'s excess/drop-down sentence, which point in slightly different directions about this policy's place in a tower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the State of New York' names a State rather than a court, then refers to 'such court' with no antecedent, and the removal savings sentence pulls against exclusivity — the term is genuinely capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in direct tension with the Service of Suit Endorsement, under which the company will submit to the jurisdiction of any court of competent jurisdiction at the insured's request, and with IX.C. on suits against the Insurer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broadly worded New York choice-of-law clause; the words themselves are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is coupled to the contested jurisdiction clause and sits against an Iowa surplus lines policy issued to an Iowa insured, so its interaction with IX.I. and the Service of Suit endorsement could be litigated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anti-waiver and anti-assignment in one sentence; 'except as provided by endorsement and attached to this Policy' is slightly garbled but clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the entire-contract statement in the Declarations and with the endorsement mechanism used throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard headings-for-convenience clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Many exclusions and endorsements are identified only by heading elsewhere (e.g. IX.G.'s list of named exclusions), a mild tension with the statement that headings form no part of the terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line reasonableness overlay on all consents; clear in principle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts provisions that give the Insurer 'sole discretion' or 'sole judgment' over approvals, notably VI.H. and VII.D., and the written-approval requirements in III.C. and V.Y.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule adding one named insured; purely mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits V.S. and V.K.; nothing in the policy contradicts the addition of Farm Nutrients LLC.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'solely with respect to their vicarious liability arising out of any named insured's direct liability' is a narrow and slightly circular formulation, and the sentence ends without punctuation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches V.A.'s statement that an additional insured has only the rights specified by endorsement; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on a 'period of interruption' and a 'Deductible Period' of three days, with 'directly attributable to' as the causal test — workable but the reporting requirement ('as soon as practicable, and during the policy period') doubles up two standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $5,000,000 sublimit equals the whole Coverage B aggregate and approaches the $7,000,000 Total Policy Aggregate in Item 4., and it is expressly made subject to those limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net profit or loss, before income taxes ... that would have been realized' is inherently a projection, and continuing payroll excludes several undefined employee categories such as 'department managers'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 'business interruption loss' and the appraisal condition, which exist precisely because this figure is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'necessary partial or complete suspension' leaves the threshold for a partial suspension undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with 'period of interruption' and 'suspension' in the same endorsement, though 'suspension' is separately defined for rented locations only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-item definitional list with an unclosed quotation mark on 'Extra expense'; the content is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Each component is separately defined in the same endorsement; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition confines business interruption to conditions covered 'for remediation costs resulting from the first-party discovery' — a compressed limitation whose effect on third-party-claim scenarios is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties this endorsement to Coverages A. and B. as rewritten by Endorsements 5, 10 and 12, so the exclusions added there (odor, fungi) silently shrink business interruption cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'for a covered location under development' is undefined and the numbering drops item 3; the enumerated expense list is otherwise closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies only to development projects, which does not obviously match the scheduled operating farm and processing sites, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'necessary to avoid or mitigate' plus 'must be incurred to actually minimize' sets two overlapping tests for the same expense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the mitigation duty in VII.D. and with 'business income'; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition gives a start point but no end point, which the separate condition IV.B. has to supply — an incomplete definition on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is completed by Endorsement 3.IV.A. and B.; read together they cohere, so the gap is cured rather than contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition tied to 'suspension' of a rented covered location; the OCR shows 'fost' for 'lost' but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 'suspension', which is limited to rented locations, matching the rental focus; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'untenantable for the purposes identified to the Insurer at the inception of the Policy' points outside the document to unquoted underwriting communications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Those inception representations are not among the documents listed in the entire-contract clause other than as part of the Application, a mild mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A counterfactual start date ('the date the operations would have begun') is inherently estimative but the rule is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the 'period of interruption' definition and IV.B.; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'remedied to the point at which normal operations could reasonably be restored' and the exclusion of losses from 'unfavorable business conditions caused by the impact of the covered pollution condition' are both fuzzy and pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second sentence may cancel much of the business income cover granted in the endorsement's insuring clause, a genuine internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional appraisal mechanism, but the closing sentence preserving the Insurer's right to deny the claim after a 'binding' appraisal is self-contradictory on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A binding appraisal also sits oddly with IX.I.'s exclusive jurisdiction clause and the Service of Suit endorsement's submission to courts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any of the individually excluded exposures identified above' has no antecedent — nothing above the sentence lists excluded exposures — so the exclusion's content is indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section VI. of the policy the phrase presumably means the policy's exclusions, but the endorsement never says so, leaving an unresolved cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two dollar figures with labels; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The catastrophe-specific $100,000 retention duplicates the Item 2.d./3.d. retention without saying whether one or two retentions apply to a single event, a small friction with II.A.'s one-retention rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is keyed to 'catastrophe management events' that 'first commence, in their entirety, on or after the inception date', a formula awkward for a media-driven event.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers only to Item 2.a. (Coverage A inception) although Coverage B has its own inception in Item 3.a., and the sublimit is layered under the Item 4. aggregate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Replacement text keeping the same 'right and the duty' phrasing subject to the Insurer's consent; internally consistent if odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces III.C., which Endorsement 6 does not touch, so the layering works; the consent requirement must be read with IX.M.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'national or regional news exposure ... reasonably likely to have a negative impact on the insured with respect to its ... reputation ... or good will' is vague at every joint.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the gateway to the catastrophe management event definition, and nothing elsewhere narrows it; no direct conflict, only inherited vagueness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger rests on 'the good faith opinion of a key executive' about future costs and future media coverage — a subjective, forward-looking test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes a covered 'pollution condition', so Endorsement 12's narrowing of that definition (odor excluded, fungi excluded) also narrows this coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition wholly dependent on the Insurer's written approval; unambiguous though one-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The approval requirement should be read with IX.M.'s no-unreasonable-withholding rule, which is consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'advising the insured with respect to minimizing potential harm ... by managing adverse media coverage' is broad but its subject-matter is identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the catastrophe management costs list and firm definition in the same endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated cost list ends in 'or other necessary response costs', a catch-all after specifics that invites ejusdem generis argument; item 2 is garbled ('mailing of materials of public relations materials').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion of 'legal defense expense' keeps it distinct from Section III and the defense sublimit; that fit is clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of titles with an approval mechanism for others; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 'responsible person' in V.Z. without conflicting; no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause mis-identifies the section it amends ('Section I1V., REPORTING AND COOPERATION' where reporting is Section VII), a mechanical error in the operative amending language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-citation matters because Section IV is Coverage Territory, so on its literal terms the endorsement replaces a subsection that does not exist in the cited section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like the business interruption version, 'any of the individually excluded exposures identified above' has no identifiable antecedent within the endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is presumably meant to import Section VI.'s exclusions, but the endorsement never says so, leaving the added exclusion's content to be inferred.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule contains plainly erroneous dates ('11/01/2074', '11/07/2014') in the retroactive-date column, and 'N/A' retroactive dates for the A&B sites is left unexplained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 8. of the Declarations points to this schedule and to Endorsement 11, and the retroactive-date entries drive the rewritten Coverage A in Endorsement 5.II — so a wrong date changes coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement grant applies only to locations 'identified with a Retroactive Date', and 'first commence, in their entirety' during or after the retroactive date remains the contestable trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.I also deletes and replaces Insuring Agreement I.A. in its entirety without preserving this retroactive-date version, so two endorsements claim to supply the operative Coverage A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amending sentence is truncated ('replaced with the') before the substituted text, and the substituted clause drops 'legal defense expense' from the per-condition limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Subsections G. and H. which the endorsement does not reproduce, and it removes defence costs from the per-condition limit while Endorsement 6.III creates a separate defence sublimit — the pieces must be assembled by the reader.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain aggregate-limit substitute keyed to Item 2.c.; nothing intrinsically ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2.c. is $9,000,000 while Item 4.'s Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000, so this 'maximum liability' statement cannot be taken at face value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It limits Coverage B to conditions 'resulting from covered operations', a term that appears nowhere else in the policy and is nowhere defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'covered operations' is undefined and the Coverage B insuring agreement contains no such limitation, this endorsement narrows the grant by a phrase the instrument cannot supply meaning for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same undefined limiter, 'all pollution conditions resulting from covered operations', governing the Coverage B aggregate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with Insuring Agreement I.B. and with the parallel Coverage A subsection D., which contains no 'covered operations' qualifier at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three exhaustion triggers are enumerated and clear; 'any applicable Aggregate Limit or Sublimit' is broad but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'Subsection E., below', which is the base policy's settlement clause that this endorsement does not reproduce, so the reader must go back to Section III.E.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward double-erosion rule; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces III.D. and is consistent with Endorsement 6.III's $2,000,000 defence sublimit and the Item 4. aggregate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sublimit figure made subject to the Total Policy Aggregate; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Endorsement 6.II.D. and IV.F., though the interaction of a 'dedicated' defence sublimit with the SIR erosion rule requires assembly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The hammer sentence is mangled — 'a settlement of any ongoing or future claim for which it is not which is acceptable to a claimant' — and it refers to covered 'loss', a term this policy never defines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and varies III.E.'s settlement clause and III.B.'s counsel-selection rules, giving two differently worded regimes for the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence fixing ninety days; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes VIII.C.'s sixty days, but the entitlement trigger in VIII.A. (cancellation or nonrenewal only) is left untouched.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanics are detailed; 'not more than two hundred percent' leaves price open but the ceiling is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Together with Endorsement 7.C. it replaces VIII.C. and D. cleanly; only the VIII.A. trigger remains unadjusted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly scrambled (the amending words, the heading and the substituted definition are interleaved) and it refers to 'third-party claims pursuant to Subsection D., above' when D. appears afterwards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 11.I. also deletes Subsection F. in its entirety and substitutes a different 'covered location' definition, so two endorsements supply competing texts for the same defined term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two paragraphs pull in different directions: the first gives the general 'claim' definition, the second limits covered claims for non-owned disposal sites, and the retroactive date is stated after the sentence that refers to it 'below'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 11.II. also deletes and replaces Subsection D., so there are two competing replacements of the 'claim' definition, each expressed as 'solely with respect to' its own coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four cumulative conditions, including that the site 'was properly permitted and licensed ... at the time of such disposal', place a historically unknowable burden on the insured but are clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers in limb 2 to a 'Schedule of Disposal Sites Endorsement' that is not attached, and the replaced exclusion O. keys off a different Retroactive Date location.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 1 excludes conditions at facilities that 'are not non-owned disposal sites', which is a double negative resting entirely on the reworked definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb 2 excludes sites that received waste before the policy period 'or any Retroactive Date identified in Section V., DEFINITIONS, Subsection D.', while the replacement 'claim' definition places that date in the endorsement itself — the cross-reference does not land cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear ninety-day/fifteen-day cancellation mechanics; the final sentences on fraud-based cancellation are stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces only paragraph 2, leaving IX.A.1's statement that the policy 'may be cancelled only by the first named insured' standing in direct contradiction to the Insurer's cancellation right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substituted grant adds transportation but retains 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period', a contestable trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes Insuring Agreement I.A. in its entirety and so, on its literal terms, wipes out Endorsement 5.II's retroactive-date version of the same subsection for the six scheduled retro-date locations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition of transportation with a clear end point at unloading; little to argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: By replacing Subsection E. it removes 'contingent transportation', which the unreplaced base Vehicles exclusion still invokes, though this endorsement also replaces that exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad vehicle exclusion with a clean carve-back for 'transportation'; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the replaced definition in Endorsement 10.II and the rewritten Coverage A; the base policy's 'contingent transportation' carve-back is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule is visibly corrupted — a column of bare numerals separated from the eleven named farms — so which entity corresponds to which numbered slot is not apparent on the face of the endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coverage for these sites depends on the schedule being determinate, since Endorsement 11.I.4 and 11.III define 'non-owned covered locations' as 'those sites identified in the Schedule above'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 3 refers to a 'Schedule of Non-Owned Disposal Sites Endorsement attached to this Policy' and to 'Subsection D., above' when D. precedes F. only in the base policy, not in this endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out barring 'any claim from or made in relation to the owner, operator, contractor of the non-owned covered location; or those of their employees' uses the vague connector 'in relation to' and lists roles without conjunctions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out may remove the very grower claims the non-owned covered location schedule appears designed to insure, and it is one of two competing replacements of the 'claim' definition (with Endorsement 8.II).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'produce certain egg related products on behalf of the insured' uses 'certain' without specifying which, and 'pursuant to an agreement with the insured' points outside the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These sites are brought into 'covered location' only through Endorsement 11.I.4, while Endorsement 8's competing definition of 'covered location' has no such limb — the two do not sit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative coverage trigger turns on 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including smoke, soot, vapors, fumes, acids, alkalis, chemicals, hazardous substances ... or waste materials' — a general term followed by industrial specifics, with a bare exclusion of 'any odor' appended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes the fungi limb while V.C. ('certified industrial hygienist') and V.Y. ('remediation costs' for fungi) survive unamended, leaving orphaned machinery in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion sweeps in 'odor' alongside fungi and legionella and applies to 'existence of, or presence of' with anti-concurrent causation, but 'odor' is nowhere defined and no carve-back is given.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fungi definition (V.L.), the certified industrial hygienist definition (V.C.) and the fungi limb of 'remediation costs' remain in the policy, so the instrument still contains fungi coverage machinery that this exclusion negates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sublimit figure with a clear scope statement for natural resource damage claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It caps a head of 'property damage' (V.X.4) at $500,000 while the per-condition limit is $2,000,000; the subordination language makes the hierarchy explicit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three figures and a retroactive date presented as a heading block; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 11/01/2003 retroactive date matches Endorsement 8's date, and the sublimits are made subject to the Declarations limits in Endorsement 13.II.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text repeats itself — 'on or after the on or after the Retroactive Date' — and 'first commences, in its entirety' is an awkward trigger for product pollution occurring after relinquishment of possession.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grant covers only 'claims' and 'legal defense expense', yet Endorsement 13.II. purports to cap 'claims, remediation costs and associated legal defense expense', so the two paragraphs describe different coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sublimit is expressed as the maximum for 'claims, remediation costs and associated legal defense expense' although the insuring clause never granted remediation costs for product pollution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch with Endorsement 13.I. is a genuine internal inconsistency about whether product-pollution remediation costs are covered at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added exclusion is extremely broad — 'arising out of any goods or products manufactured, sold or distributed by an insured' — with a carve-back only for 'product pollution', so its reach against an egg producer's ordinary operations is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the insured's business is producing egg products at the scheduled and non-owned covered locations, this exclusion arguably swallows much of Coverages A and B, leaving only a $1,000,000 sublimited carve-back.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'arises out of the use of a product ... provided that such use occurs after the insured has relinquished possession' is workable, but 'products do not include waste products' draws an unexplained line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The waste/product line matters because the transportation endorsement covers 'the insured's waste or products', so the two endorsements treat the same items differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short sanctions clause using 'us' where the policy elsewhere says 'the Insurer', but its operation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The first-person voice is inconsistent with the rest of the form's third-person drafting; no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the company will submit to the jurisdiction of any court of competent jurisdiction' at the insured's request is open-ended, and whether it is merely a service/consent provision or a venue right is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points squarely against IX.I.'s 'exclusive jurisdiction of the State of New York', and Endorsement 15's own non-variation sentence does not resolve which prevails.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'OTHER THAN AS ABOVE STATED' is the hinge: it both preserves and overrides policy terms depending on how far 'as above stated' reaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its function is precisely to mediate between the service of suit provisions and IX.I./IX.J., so its effect on the exclusive New York forum clause is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statement that only signatures representing 'the company named on the first page of the Declarations' apply is clear, though the surrounding text is OCR-corrupted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature block names two companies (Illinois Union and Westchester Surplus Lines) while the Declarations name only Illinois Union, a mismatch this clause is drafted to cure.
